problem: The observability package owns node trace construction but also imports Lifecycle state validation and Persistence SQLite/StoreProvider implementations. Those hidden implementation dependencies reverse the intended direction and keep observability in the core SCC.

options.name: Keep hidden validator and StoreProvider lookups
options.correctness: Preserves behavior but keeps observability coupled to lifecycle and persistence.

options.name: Inject validator and trace repository; move SQLite trace implementation to persistence
options.correctness: Preserves all trace/state-contract behavior while making observability dependency-neutral and composition explicit.
options.migration: Add neutral protocols, move TraceLogger implementation, pass validator/trace repository from lifecycle graph, update provider and metrics.
options.rollback: Restore hidden lookups and old TraceLogger owner.
options.verification: Boundary/SCC counterexample, trace storage tests, state contract tests, full Quick.

options.name: Hide imports behind dynamic proxies
options.correctness: Could improve static graph without removing runtime coupling.

rejected_reasons.keep-hidden-lookups: It preserves the wrong dependency direction.
rejected_reasons.dynamic-proxy: It manufactures graph improvement while retaining hidden global coupling.

deletions: Delete the concrete SQLite TraceLogger from observability and delete all observability imports/lookups of lifecycle and persistence.
unknowns: The remaining 5-package SCC remains open debt.
State/Loop simplification and real-model certification remain future targets.
selected_responsibilities: observability owns neutral event construction, redaction, correlation, metrics contracts and timers.
lifecycle owns state validation and explicitly supplies it to debug wrappers.
persistence owns the concrete SQLite trace repository and StoreProvider construction.
preserved_hard_invariants: Graph node trace payloads and State Contract strict/audit behavior remain unchanged.
Trace table schema, correlation, redaction and query behavior remain unchanged.
All prior removed packages remain outside the main SCC.
The dependency debt baseline is not edited.
cutover_strategy: Record expected-red, introduce explicit ports, move the concrete trace store without logic changes, update lifecycle/provider composition, then run complete verification.
acceptance_claims: observability imports neither lifecycle nor persistence and has no concrete SQLite store.
Lifecycle passes the canonical validator and configured TraceRepository explicitly.
The current SCC member count is at most 5 and observability plus all prior removed packages remain outside it.
All state-contract, trace storage, lifecycle, frontend and browser tests remain green.
